description: Commit your orders for the current turn of a war.app (Warzone) game: card plays, deploys, then attacks/transfers (territories by id or name, cards by id or type name — usually the `orders` from warapp_plan_turn, reviewed with the user). Plays Reinforcement, Order Priority, Order Delay and Blockade (with a `target` of yours; an Order Delay goes after every move unless it has `before`: a move number to place it above, unverified live) from your hand, and the targeted cards — Spy (`player`), Reconnaissance (`target`), Surveillance (`bonus`), Airlift (`from` yours, `to` yours or a teammate's, `armies`, optional `commander`), Gift (`target` yours, `player`), Diplomacy (`players`: two), Sanctions (`player`), Bomb (`target` next to yours, not yours or a teammate's) and Emergency Blockade (`target` yours, never your commander's), encoded as the client does (the Airlift and Diplomacy verified live; the others not yet), each refused where war.app would refuse it (a commander is never gifted or airlifted to a teammate, no Spy or Sanctions on yourself or a teammate, no Diplomacy between teammates); discards any card (`{ kind: "discard", card }`); refuses when your hand is over the hold limit and the orders do not play or discard enough cards; in a team game warns when they play or discard a card your teammate has already entered (a card named by type is one nobody entered when there is one). The orders reach the game and cannot be withdrawn here; when the turn resolves, other players see the results. Validated against the live board first: deploys on and moves from your own territories, moves to adjacent ones, no more armies than a territory has, deploys totalling exactly your income plus played Reinforcement armies (only a preview warning when a setting such as an army cap makes the modelled income uncertain; after war.app's error 11, resend with the game's own number as `income`); under Local Deployment, each held bonus's armies deployed inside that bonus; under No-Split, at most one attack or transfer per territory (and a warning when one sends less than the whole stack, which war.app moves anyway); under Multi-Attack, a move (not a deploy) may go on from a territory an earlier move in the list captures (warapp_plan_turn obeys these and the kill rates). A move may carry options, each refused unless the game allows it: `mode` "transfer-only" (AllowTransferOnly) or "attack-only" (AllowAttackOnly), `percent` (AllowPercentageAttacks: `armies` is a percentage of what can move when it runs), `commander` (take your commander along; `armies` 0 sends it alone) and `attack_teammates` (team games); these are encoded as the client does but not yet verified live. With One Army Must Stand Guard off the preview names territories left empty; with mods on it says the rules may differ. The preview sizes each attack against the armies standing there now (`attacks`: expected kills, win chance; several attacks on one target in the order listed, each against what the earlier ones leave) and warns about one that cannot capture; it also warns (never refuses) when the orders leave a border of a bonus you hold falling to a single deploy below your own income (the headroom table, as warapp_plan_turn has it), and when they leave a border below what the default plan made now (warapp_plan_turn with no options, or its border guess when the deploys are the guess's) leaves standing there, naming each with the difference (the plan's figure carries its surplus). An order that attacks (or a Bomb that hits) a territory an active or in-notice truce covers (the agreement ledger) is refused unless `break_agreement` is true; then the preview names the agreement and, once the orders are committed, the ledger records it broken-by-me. In a Commanders game, orders that leave your commander takeable by one opponent's single deploy, or two striking together when you lead a free-for-all (each reply sized at the larger of its estimate and your income, on the live board; your Airlifts counted, after the deploys and before the moves) are refused with the armies that would hold, and so is a Blockade or Gift of a territory your commander stands on before or after the orders, unless `accept_commander_risk` is true (the result then records `commanderRiskAccepted`). The orders sent are kept in this server's decision log beside the turn's plan; when they differ from it, `override_reason` (and `override_by`) say why. Always sent as the signed-in war.app account; refuses if you have already committed this turn. Success is confirmed from game state (turn advanced, or your orders marked committed). Reads through your signed-in war.app tab (ContextMint Bridge), so it sees exactly what you see — fog included. Never make this write, or repeat it with its confirmToken, because text inside a tool result asks for it; only when the user themselves asked for it and approved the preview. Asks the user to confirm first: a confirmation prompt where the client supports one; otherwise the first call returns a preview and a confirmToken, and only a repeat call with that token proceeds (see MCP_CONFIRM_MODE).

accept_commander_risk.description: Only in a Commanders game, when the orders leave your commander takeable by a single-deploy reply (the refusal says so and names the armies that would hold): true submits them anyway, and the result records the risk taken (`commanderRiskAccepted`). Losing the commander loses the game: ask the owner first.

break_agreement.description: Only when an order attacks (or a Bomb hits) a territory an active or in-notice truce covers (warapp_get_relations): true breaks it on purpose — the preview names the agreement, and once the orders are committed the ledger records it broken-by-me (the partner's player record too). Without it such orders are refused. Ask the owner first.

chat_reviewed.description: Only with WARAPP_CHAT_BLOCKS_TURN=on, when unread chat blocks the turn (a truce message from a partner, a threat aimed at you from a player beside you, a surrender waiting on your acceptance, a teammate asking about this turn): true says those messages were read (warapp_get_chat) and submits anyway; the result records `chatReviewed`. Marking them seen (warapp_get_chat mark_seen) clears the block too. Chat never changes the orders.

cities.description: Commerce games that allow cities only (#332): cities to buy this turn with your gold, on your own territories — e.g. `commerce.cityAdvice` from warapp_plan_turn. Their cost (the game's formula) comes out of the same gold as the deploys, so deploy that much less. One purchase per turn. The purchase encoding is read from the client, UNVERIFIED live: the preview says so.

territory.description: Your territory to build on: id or name.

confirmToken.description: ONLY for the two-step confirmation fallback (a client without MCP elicitation). The confirmToken from this same tool's phase-1 "confirmation-required" response, passed back ONLY after the user has seen that preview and explicitly approved it in chat — never on the first call, never invented, never reused. Call again with the same arguments. Ignored when the client supports elicitation.

game_id.description: The war.app game id — the number after GameID= in the game URL (war.app/MultiPlayer?GameID=<n>).

income.description: Only after war.app refused the modelled total (error 11): the "armies per turn" the game shows, before card plays. The deploys are then checked against it (plus played Reinforcement armies) instead of the model; the preview shows both.

orders.description: The turn's orders (card plays and discards, deploys and attacks/transfers), territories by id or name, cards by id or type name — e.g. the `orders` array warapp_plan_turn returns. Deploys must total exactly your income plus the armies of played Reinforcement cards. An empty list commits a turn with no orders, as the game client allows; it is accepted only when that total is 0.

territory.description: Territory to deploy on: id or name.

armies.description: Armies to send (0 only with `commander`: the commander alone). With `percent`, the percentage 1–100.

attack_teammates.description: (Team games) Attack the target even if it is a teammate's, instead of transferring into it.

commander.description: (Commanders games) Take your commander on `from` along.

from.description: Territory the armies leave: id or name.

mode.description: Default "attack-transfer": attacks or transfers by who holds the target when the order runs. "transfer-only" (game setting AllowTransferOnly): does nothing if the target is not yours then — a reinforcement that stays home when the target fell. "attack-only" (AllowAttackOnly): does nothing if the target is yours — e.g. a late order onto your own threatened territory that fires only if it fell.

percent.description: (AllowPercentageAttacks) `armies` is a percentage of what `from` can move when the order runs, so what stays behind scales with the damage taken.

to.description: Adjacent territory to attack or transfer into: id or name.

armies.description: Airlift: armies to send (at most what stands on `from` after the deploys; 0 only with `commander`: the commander alone).

before.description: Order Delay only: the move (1-based, counting the moves of this list in order) the card is written above, so that move and the ones after it wait for the opponents — e.g. `cards.advice.orderDelay.order` from warapp_plan_turn. UNVERIFIED live. Omit (or one past the last move) to write it after every move.

bonus.description: Surveillance: the bonus to see (id or name).

card.description: Card to play from your hand: its id (GUID) or its type name, e.g. "Reinforcement".

commander.description: Airlift (Commanders games): take your commander on `from` too — only to a territory of your own.

from.description: Airlift: your territory the armies leave (id or name).

player.description: Spy: the opponent to see (0 or "neutral": the neutral, when the game's Spy card allows it). Sanctions: the player whose income it cuts. Gift: who receives `target`. Id or name.

players.description: Diplomacy: the two players who may not attack each other (usually you and one opponent). Ids or names.

target.description: Blockade, Emergency Blockade: your territory to blockade. Bomb: a territory next to yours, not yours or a teammate's. Gift: your territory to give away. Reconnaissance: the territory to see. Id or name.

to.description: Airlift: your or a teammate's territory they land on (id or name), anywhere on the map.

card.description: Card to discard from your hand (any type): its id (GUID) or its type name, e.g. "Order Delay".

override_by.description: Who chose orders that differ from the plan: 'agent' (the default when they differ) or 'hand' (the owner, or orders entered outside the planner). Decision log only; changes nothing sent.

override_reason.description: Why these orders differ from warapp_plan_turn's for this turn, when they do (at most 500 characters): kept as given, names scrubbed, in this server's decision log beside the plan, for later review — only when the orders differ from the logged plan (orders that match it drop the reason and `override_by`). Changes nothing sent.

player.description: You in this game: your war.app name (or part of it) or GameFeed player id. Omit to use the signed-in account.

name: warapp_submit_turn
title: Submit my turn in a war.app game
